boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Luther College
boards.description: Ten currently documented evening destinations in Decorah, selected for under-21-safe food, coffee, shopping, and activities.

cards.title: Pizza Hut on Short Street
cards.subtitle: 1002 Short St, Decorah
cards.notes: Use the official ordering page to confirm service type, then plan carryout or delivery before the listed 11 p.m. close; Friday and Saturday list midnight.
cards.short_summary: A Short Street pizza option with the latest published food hours in town.
cards.evidence_claim: The Decorah location lists delivery and carryout until 11 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and midnight Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists delivery/carryout 9 a.m.–11 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and 9 a.m.–midnight Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Culver’s on Short Street
cards.subtitle: 904 Short St, Decorah
cards.notes: Check the daily flavor and head to the Short Street location before its published 10 p.m. close; lobby, dine-in, curbside, and drive-thru share the listed hours.
cards.short_summary: An evening food-and-dessert stop with daily service to 10 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Culver’s lists its Decorah lobby, dine-in, curbside, and drive-thru as open daily from 10:30 a.m. to 10 p.m.
cards.source_title: Culver's of Decorah, IA — Short St
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists daily lobby, dine-in, curbside, and drive-thru hours of 10:30 a.m.–10 p.m.

cards.title: Casey’s on College Drive
cards.subtitle: 401 College Dr, Decorah
cards.notes: For a later convenience-store stop, use the official page to place pickup before 9:30 p.m.; the store itself lists service until 10 p.m. daily.
cards.short_summary: A College Drive convenience stop with pizza and snack options.
cards.evidence_claim: Casey’s lists the 401 College Drive store open 6 a.m.–10 p.m. daily, with pickup through 9:30 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists store hours 6 a.m.–10 p.m. daily and pickup 6 a.m.–9:30 p.m. daily.

cards.title: Walmart Supercenter on Old Stage Road
cards.subtitle: 1798 Old Stage Rd, Decorah
cards.notes: Use this option for practical groceries or essentials when earlier venues have closed; the store page lists every day from 6 a.m. through 11 p.m.
cards.short_summary: A late-evening essentials and grocery destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Walmart lists the Decorah Supercenter at 1798 Old Stage Road open daily from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Official store page lists Monday–Sunday store hours of 6 a.m.–11 p.m.

cards.title: Sugar Bowl at The Landing
cards.subtitle: 211 College Dr, Decorah
cards.notes: For an evening ice-cream outing during its stated season, go to the Landing location before 10 p.m.; the Water Street shop is listed as seasonal and closed.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal College Drive ice-cream stop open later than its downtown counterpart.
cards.evidence_claim: Sugar Bowl lists its Landing location at 211 College Drive as open daily from 11 a.m. to 10 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Sugar Bowl at The Landing open daily 11 a.m.–10 p.m. and identifies a March 20–November 1 season.

cards.title: Don Jose on East Water Street
cards.subtitle: 201 E Water St, Decorah
cards.notes: Check the listed day before walking downtown: dinner service runs to 9 p.m. most nights and to 9:30 p.m. Friday and Saturday; Monday is closed.
cards.short_summary: A downtown dinner destination with documented 9:30 p.m. weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Don Jose lists service until 9 p.m. Tuesday–Thursday and Sunday, and until 9:30 p.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official restaurant site lists Tuesday–Thursday and Sunday until 9 p.m.; Friday and Saturday until 9:30 p.m.; Monday closed.

cards.title: Mabe’s Pizza on Water Street
cards.subtitle: 110 E Water St, Decorah
cards.notes: Order dine-in, takeout, or delivery from the official site; Friday and Saturday hours extend to 10 p.m., while Sunday through Thursday list a 9 p.m. close.
cards.short_summary: A downtown pizza stop with 10 p.m. Friday and Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Mabe’s lists dine-in, takeout, and delivery; it is open until 10 p.m. Friday and Saturday and until 9 p.m. Sunday–Thursday.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Sunday–Thursday 11 a.m.–9 p.m. and Friday–Saturday 11 a.m.–10 p.m.

cards.title: King Pin Entertainment Center
cards.subtitle: 400 Heivly St, Decorah
cards.notes: Reserve a lane or check arcade availability before heading over; the venue lists lanes and arcade to 10 p.m. most open days and midnight Friday–Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A bowling-and-arcade option with the board’s latest activity hours.
cards.evidence_claim: King Pin lists lanes and arcade until 10 p.m. Sunday and Tuesday–Thursday, and until midnight Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: King Pin Entertainment Center — Bowling Reservation
cards.access_notes: Official page lists lanes and arcade 11 a.m.–10 p.m. Sunday and Tuesday–Thursday, and 11 a.m.–midnight Friday–Saturday; Monday is closed.

cards.title: Subway on Short Street
cards.subtitle: 809 Short St, Decorah
cards.notes: Use the official store page for pickup or delivery planning; its posted hours run to 10 p.m. every day, making it a reliable late sandwich option.
cards.short_summary: A daily 10 p.m. sandwich stop on the Short Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Subway at 809 Short Street lists store hours of 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. every day.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists Monday–Sunday store hours of 8 a.m.–10 p.m.

cards.title: Impact Coffee on Water Street
cards.subtitle: 101 W Water St, Decorah
cards.notes: Choose Thursday through Saturday for the later coffee-bar schedule, which runs to 9 p.m.; verify seasonal events separately and use the posted hours for timing.
cards.short_summary: A Water Street coffee stop open into the evening three days a week.
cards.evidence_claim: Impact Coffee lists coffee-bar hours until 9 p.m. Thursday, Friday, and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists Thursday and Friday 6:30 a.m.–9 p.m. and Saturday 7 a.m.–9 p.m.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Luther College places with documented ways to study, create, gather, eat, or be active together.

cards.title: Preus Library
cards.subtitle: Three levels of open and private study space
cards.notes: Choose an open table for a group project, or reserve a study room when you need a smaller setting; quieter areas are on the upper and lower levels.
cards.short_summary: A campus research hub with shared tables, private rooms, computers, and digital-media support.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther states that all three floors have open study areas and private study rooms, and identifies the building as a central resource for campus activities.
cards.access_notes: Library hours and room availability vary; consult the library before visiting.

cards.title: Dahl Centennial Union
cards.subtitle: Dining, student organizations, services, and a student-art gallery
cards.notes: Meet a classmate for food, stop by the student-art gallery, or use the building as a practical rendezvous point before handling campus errands.
cards.short_summary: The central union combines dining with student-organization and support-service offices.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther describes Dahl Centennial Union as the central campus hub and lists dining, a student-organization office suite, student artwork gallery, and student-life offices.
cards.access_notes: Dining and offices have separate schedules; check current campus information before going.

cards.title: Oneota Market
cards.subtitle: Dahl Centennial Union, first floor
cards.notes: Use the seating area to catch up with someone between classes or work on homework over a snack; purchase is required for food or drinks.
cards.short_summary: A bright Union dining spot with room to eat, talk, or work between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther says Oneota Market is on the first floor of Dahl Centennial Union and is a place to grab food, chat with friends, or catch up on homework.
cards.access_notes: Food and beverages require purchase; verify current dining availability before visiting.

cards.title: Center for Faith and Life
cards.subtitle: Main hall, recital hall, and multifaith meditation room
cards.notes: Check the event calendar for a concert, lecture, recital, or worship service; for quiet individual reflection, use the multifaith meditation room.
cards.short_summary: A performance and gathering venue that also includes a room for individual prayer and meditation.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther identifies the Center for Faith and Life as its main performance hall and says its recital hall hosts lectures, panels, meetings, and performances.
cards.source_title: Center for Faith and Life | Luther College
cards.access_notes: Event attendance and ticketing vary; Luther states the multifaith meditation room is accessible 24/7 via an outside entrance.

cards.title: Center for the Arts
cards.subtitle: Art, dance, theatre, and the Wigley-Fleming Fine Arts Gallery
cards.notes: Visit the Wigley-Fleming Fine Arts Gallery to see current work, or attend a listed student or faculty production in the Jewel Theatre.
cards.short_summary: A visual- and performing-arts building with studios, rehearsal spaces, theatre, and gallery.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther says the Center for the Arts houses art, dance, and theatre facilities and that its gallery displays work by students, faculty, and visiting artists.
cards.source_title: Center for the Arts | Luther College
cards.access_notes: Studios and productions may be class-, department-, or ticket-specific; confirm access before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Gerdin Fieldhouse for Athletics and Wellness
cards.title: Gerdin Fieldhouse
cards.subtitle: Courts, indoor turf, fitness, and recreation facilities
cards.notes: See whether an open recreation or athletics event fits your schedule, then use the listed courts, track, or fitness resources according to campus access rules.
cards.short_summary: Luther’s athletics and recreation hub, with courts, an indoor turf room, track, and fitness center.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther describes Gerdin Fieldhouse and adjoining facilities as the campus hub for athletics and recreation, listing courts, an indoor turf practice room, track, and fitness center.
cards.source_title: Gerdin Fieldhouse for Athletics and Wellness | Luther College
cards.access_notes: Facility access and event schedules vary; follow current athletics and recreation guidance.

cards.title: Aquatic Center
cards.subtitle: Part of the Gerdin Fieldhouse athletics-and-wellness complex
cards.notes: Look for current open-swim or recreation access before heading over, and follow posted pool rules while sharing the facility with other users.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus aquatic facility connected to Luther’s central recreation complex.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther lists the Aquatic Center among the adjoining facilities that make the Gerdin Fieldhouse complex the hub for athletics and recreation.
cards.source_title: Gerdin Fieldhouse for Athletics and Wellness | Luther College
cards.access_notes: Pool access and programming vary; verify current availability and eligibility before visiting.

cards.title: Library Lawn
cards.subtitle: Central greenspace beside Preus Library
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or meet a group outdoors when the weather cooperates; check the campus calendar for organized activities scheduled on the lawn.
cards.short_summary: A central outdoor gathering area beside Preus Library used for recreation programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther’s recreation page lists Library Lawn as a location for scheduled lawn games, cricket, flag football, kickball, and pickleball-related activities.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use depends on weather and scheduled activities; follow posted campus guidance.

cards.title: Tennis Courts
cards.subtitle: Lower-campus outdoor athletics area
cards.notes: Check whether courts are available, then join a scheduled recreation session or bring a partner for a campus-appropriate game of pickleball or tennis.
cards.short_summary: A named lower-campus court area used in Luther recreation programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther’s recreation services page identifies the Tennis Courts as the location for scheduled pickleball, and the campus map lists Tennis Courts as a named destination.
cards.access_notes: Court availability may be affected by athletics or recreation schedules; verify before playing.

cards.title: Anderson Prairie
cards.subtitle: Named campus natural area
cards.notes: Take a daylight walk on the maintained route with a classmate, pause to observe the landscape, and leave the area as you found it.
cards.short_summary: A named Luther campus prairie destination for a low-key outdoor reset.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther’s campus map lists Anderson Prairie as a named campus destination, and its visit page depicts people walking on a mowed prairie path.
cards.access_notes: Use marked paths and observe campus natural-area guidance; conditions vary by season.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-admission activities at Luther College and in Decorah, selected from public institutional and government sources.

cards.title: Tune Up at the Bike Fixit Station
cards.subtitle: Preus Library, Luther College
cards.notes: Bring a bike that needs attention, use the free pump and tools, and make a practical meet-up before riding elsewhere around campus.
cards.short_summary: A free self-service bike-maintenance stop beside Preus Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther College states that the Bike Fixit Station provides a free tire pump and tools for all Luther cyclists.
cards.source_title: Bike Share and Bike Fixit Station | Luther College
cards.access_notes: The station is beside the library's south-side bike racks; bring your own bicycle.

cards.title: Meet at Preus Library
cards.subtitle: 575 Library St., Luther College
cards.notes: Pick a table for a quiet catch-up, browse materials together, or use the public workstations without planning a purchase.
cards.short_summary: A campus library setting with posted building hours and public-facing computer access.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther lists Preus Library's building hours and states that its public kiosk workstations do not require a Luther Norse Key.
cards.source_title: Computer Labs and Classrooms | Luther College
cards.access_notes: Use during posted library hours; library schedules vary by term and break period.

cards.title: Visit Hanson Vesterheim Commons
cards.subtitle: Vesterheim campus, Decorah
cards.notes: Meet under the timber canopy, look through the welcome center and gallery if open, then continue into the adjacent outdoor heritage grounds.
cards.short_summary: A daily-open community space connected to Vesterheim Heritage Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Vesterheim states that Hanson Vesterheim Commons is open daily from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. with no admission charge.
cards.source_title: Vesterheim Commons Is Open | Vesterheim Norwegian-American Museum
cards.access_notes: Open daily 9 a.m.–5 p.m. according to Vesterheim; special-gallery availability can vary.

cards.title: See Decorah Ice Cave
cards.subtitle: Van Peenen Memorial Park, Decorah
cards.notes: Take the stairs to the cave entrance with a friend, use careful footing, and leave time to observe seasonal ice from a safe distance.
cards.short_summary: A named geological preserve with a narrow limestone cave passage.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa DNR states that Decorah Ice Cave is open to the public free of charge.
cards.source_title: Decorah Ice Cave State Preserve | Iowa Department of Natural Resources
cards.access_notes: Footing can be hazardous and rocks may be loose; follow DNR cautions and do not disturb ice or rock.

cards.title: Watch Trout at the Hatchery
cards.subtitle: Decorah, Iowa
cards.notes: Walk the raceways, read the interpretive plaques, and use the picnic shelter for a conversation break without buying fish feed.
cards.short_summary: A public hatchery with raceways, interpretation, and a year-round shelter.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa DNR states that the Chuck Gipp Decorah Fish Hatchery is open to the public 365 days a year from sunrise to sunset.
cards.source_title: New watershed plan improves water quality at the Chuck Gipp Decorah Fishery Hatchery | Iowa DNR
cards.access_notes: Public access is sunrise to sunset; fish feed is optional and is not needed for a visit.

cards.title: Walk a Section of Trout Run Trail
cards.subtitle: Starting near the Decorah Fish Hatchery
cards.notes: Choose a daylight out-and-back segment, walk at a conversational pace, and use the hatchery area as a simple start and finish point.
cards.short_summary: An 11-mile Decorah-area trail for a flexible walk or roll.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa DNR identifies Trout Run Trail as an 11-mile route through Decorah and says the hatchery is a starting point for it.
cards.source_title: New watershed plan improves water quality at the Chuck Gipp Decorah Fishery Hatchery | Iowa DNR
cards.access_notes: Use daylight, account for weather, and share the multiuse trail courteously.

cards.title: Walk the Community Prairie
cards.subtitle: Decorah, Iowa
cards.notes: Follow the mowed walking paths, pause at the butterfly garden, and pick a short loop that fits the season and your group’s pace.
cards.short_summary: A city prairie with walking paths and a seasonal butterfly garden.
cards.evidence_claim: Decorah Parks and Recreation describes the Decorah Community Prairie as having mowed walking paths, a butterfly garden, and a community garden.
cards.source_title: Park Amenities & Descriptions | Decorah Parks and Recreation
cards.access_notes: Use the paths and respect seasonal planting areas and any posted site rules.

cards.title: Hang Out at Phelps Park
cards.subtitle: Park Street, Decorah
cards.notes: Bring a conversation, a book, or a game you already own, then use the overlooks, picnic area, playground, and hiking trail at your own pace.
cards.short_summary: Decorah’s first park, with a playground, shelters, lookouts, and trail.
cards.evidence_claim: Decorah Parks and Recreation identifies Phelps Park as the city's first park and lists its playground, picnic shelters, stone-walled lookouts, fountain, and hiking trail.
cards.source_title: Park Amenities & Descriptions | Decorah Parks and Recreation
cards.access_notes: Open public-park areas are suitable for a no-purchase visit; separately reservable facilities may have fees.

cards.entity_name: Dunning's Spring Waterfall and Stone Arch Bridge
cards.title: Walk to Dunning’s Spring Waterfall
cards.subtitle: Dunning's Spring Park, Decorah
cards.notes: Start at the park entrance, take the short approach to the waterfall and bridge, and use marked public paths for a low-key outdoor stop.
cards.short_summary: A named Decorah waterfall and stone bridge within the city’s park system.
cards.evidence_claim: Decorah Parks and Recreation's trail guide identifies Dunning's Spring Waterfall and Stone Arch Bridge and gives directions from Dunning's Spring Park.
cards.source_title: Decorah Parks and Trails Guide | Decorah Parks and Recreation
cards.access_notes: Stay on established public paths and check site conditions after storms or seasonal changes.

cards.entity_name: Carl Selland Wayside Park Ice Rink
cards.title: Skate at Carl Selland Wayside Park
cards.subtitle: Decorah, Iowa
cards.notes: When the rink is posted open, bring skates, meet in the warming house, and keep the hang simple by following the shared-rink rules.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal public ice-rink and warming-house activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Decorah Parks and Recreation states that use of the Carl Selland Wayside Park rink and warming house is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Decorah Parks and Recreation Rules and Regulations
cards.access_notes: Seasonal only; check the entrance sign or Parks and Recreation for ice-open status and warming-house hours.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Luther College study environments, from library rooms and workstations to campus and residence-hall lounges.

cards.entity_name: Preus Library Upper-Level Open Study Area
cards.title: Preus Library’s Upper-Level Open Study Area
cards.subtitle: Preus Library · upper level
cards.notes: Bring independent reading or writing to the upper level, where Preus documents open study areas and notes that upper levels tend to be quieter.
cards.short_summary: A quieter open-floor option above Preus Library’s main level.
cards.evidence_claim: Preus Library has Wi-Fi-enabled open study areas on all three floors; its upper and lower levels tend to be quieter.
cards.access_notes: Use during posted Preus Library building hours; check the library hours page for daily and term schedules.

cards.entity_name: Preus Library Lower-Level Open Study Area
cards.title: Preus Library’s Lower-Level Open Study Area
cards.subtitle: Preus Library · lower level
cards.notes: Set up on the lower level for focused solo work. The library identifies open study areas there and describes lower levels as tending to be quieter.
cards.short_summary: Open lower-level seating in Preus Library’s quieter zone.
cards.evidence_claim: Preus Library provides Wi-Fi-enabled open study areas on all three floors, and says its lower level tends to be quieter.
cards.access_notes: Use during posted Preus Library building hours; check the library hours page for daily and term schedules.

cards.title: Preus Library’s Individual Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Preus Library
cards.notes: Ask at the circulation desk for a key when you need a contained study setting; the library lists keys for individual and group study rooms.
cards.short_summary: Key-access individual rooms for focused library work.
cards.evidence_claim: Preus Library offers individual study rooms, and its circulation desk provides keys for individual and group study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Room keys are obtained through the Circulation Desk; use during posted library hours.

cards.title: Preus Library’s Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Preus Library
cards.notes: Coordinate a project meeting, then obtain a room key from circulation. Luther lists small group rooms among the library’s study facilities.
cards.short_summary: A library room option for project partners and small groups.
cards.evidence_claim: Preus Library has small group study rooms, and the Circulation Desk provides keys for group study rooms.
cards.source_title: Preus Library | Luther College Virtual Tour
cards.access_notes: Obtain a group-study-room key from the Circulation Desk; use during posted library hours.

cards.title: Preus Library Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Preus Library · main level
cards.notes: Use the main-level computer lab when your coursework needs a campus workstation. The virtual tour identifies it as the college’s largest computer lab.
cards.short_summary: Main-level workstations in Luther’s largest computer lab.
cards.evidence_claim: Preus Library’s main level contains a computer lab, described by Luther as the largest computer lab on campus.
cards.source_title: Preus Library | Luther College Virtual Tour
cards.access_notes: Located on Preus Library’s main level; library building hours govern access.

cards.title: Digital Media Center Lab
cards.subtitle: Preus Library · lower level
cards.notes: Choose the lab for photo, video, or media-editing coursework. Luther says the lab is an open learning space with high-end Macs for these projects.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level media-work lab for digital projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The Digital Media Center’s lower-level multimedia lab is an open learning space with high-end Macs for photo, media, and video editing.
cards.access_notes: The DMC Lab is available whenever Preus Library is open; the DMC Studio requires an appointment.

cards.title: Language Learning Center
cards.subtitle: Main Building 215
cards.notes: Use Main 215 for language coursework or a small-group session. The center provides films, print resources, a computer lab, and private study areas.
cards.short_summary: Language resources and study areas in Main 215.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther’s Language Learning Center in Main 215 offers private study rooms and areas, a computer lab, films, print resources, and space for small groups.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday through Friday; Luther states students are welcome whenever the door is open.

cards.title: Koren Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: Koren Hall
cards.notes: Head to Koren when you want a study lounge near social-science classrooms and offices. Luther explicitly states the lounge is available to all students.
cards.short_summary: An all-student study lounge in historic Koren Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Koren Hall has a study lounge available for all students.
cards.access_notes: Located in Koren Hall; no separate public lounge hours are stated on the source page.

cards.title: Brunsdale Lounge
cards.subtitle: Between Miller and Dieseth Halls
cards.notes: If you live in the Towers, use Brunsdale’s study setting between Miller and Dieseth. Luther identifies it as a social meeting place and study location.
cards.short_summary: A Towers lounge with dedicated study use.
cards.evidence_claim: Brunsdale Lounge connects Miller and Dieseth Halls and functions as both a social meeting place and a study location.
cards.source_title: Miller and Dieseth Halls (Towers) | Luther College
cards.access_notes: Located within the Miller–Dieseth Towers residence-hall complex; confirm building access with Residence Life.

cards.title: Farwell Hall Top-Floor Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: Farwell Hall · top floor
cards.notes: For a longer indoor work session, use Farwell’s top-floor study lounge, which Luther documents with a kitchen, fireplace, and scenic view.
cards.short_summary: A top-floor residence-hall lounge designed for study and social use.
cards.evidence_claim: Farwell Hall has a large top-floor study/social lounge with a kitchen, fireplace, and scenic view.
cards.access_notes: Inside Farwell Hall; confirm residence-hall guest and building-access rules with Residence Life.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along Water Street, Decorah’s downtown corridor off the Luther College campus.

cards.entity_name: Vesterheim Norwegian-American Museum & Folk Art School
cards.title: Vesterheim’s artifact collection
cards.subtitle: Water Street corridor — 502 W. Water Street
cards.notes: Walk Water Street to Vesterheim and use its galleries and historic buildings to explore Norwegian-American immigration and folk art.
cards.short_summary: A museum and folk-art school with artifacts, historic buildings, and year-round classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Vesterheim at 502 W. Water Street holds 33,000 artifacts, 12 historic buildings, and offers year-round folk-art classes.
cards.source_title: Vesterheim Norwegian-American Museum & Folk Art School — Visit Decorah
cards.access_notes: Check Vesterheim’s official visitor information for current gallery and class access.

cards.title: Oneota’s local-food shelves
cards.subtitle: Water Street corridor — 312 W. Water Street
cards.notes: Stop into the Water Street co-op to browse organic, local, bulk, and minimally packaged food and household goods.
cards.short_summary: A cooperatively owned grocery specializing in organic, local, and sustainably produced products.
cards.evidence_claim: Oneota Community Food Co-op is a cooperatively owned grocery at 312 West Water Street specializing in organic, local, and sustainably produced products.
cards.source_title: Oneota Community Food Co-op — Visit Decorah
cards.access_notes: Retail purchases are optional; confirm current store access before visiting.

cards.title: Water Street Deli’s take-out menu
cards.subtitle: Water Street corridor — 301 W. Water Street
cards.notes: Use the deli as a take-out stop for its seasonal hot and cold menu, pantry goods, and sliced meats and cheeses.
cards.short_summary: A take-out deli with seasonal prepared food and a crafted pantry selection.
cards.evidence_claim: Water Street Deli at 301 W. Water Street offers seasonal hot and cold options, pantry goods, and take-out service.
cards.access_notes: Take-out only, according to the listed business information.

cards.title: Kanpai’s soda and candy counter
cards.subtitle: Water Street corridor — 404 W. Water Street
cards.notes: Browse bottled sodas, specialty candy, popcorn, and root beer at this Water Street shop; staff can explain Ramune bottles.
cards.short_summary: A soda shop with specialty candy, popcorn, root beer, and marble-sealed Ramune.
cards.evidence_claim: Kanpai Soda Shop is located at 404 W. Water Street and sells soda choices, specialty candy, popcorn, and root beer.
cards.access_notes: Purchases are optional; verify current shop access before making a trip.

cards.title: Games XP’s gaming room
cards.subtitle: Water Street corridor — 105 E. Water Street
cards.notes: Visit the shop’s gaming room for its couches, televisions, vintage arcade machines, and pinball; TV use has a rental fee.
cards.short_summary: A game shop with video games, records, arcade machines, pinball, and a gaming room.
cards.evidence_claim: Games XP at 105 East Water Street has a gaming room with couches, seven TVs, vintage arcade machines, and pinball; the room is otherwise free to hang out in.
cards.access_notes: The listing states that TV use has a rental fee; other gaming-room hangout access is described as free.

cards.title: Dragonfly’s author-event shelf
cards.subtitle: Water Street corridor — 112 W. Water Street
cards.notes: Browse across fiction, mysteries, history, cookbooks, and children’s books, then check the store’s current author-event information.
cards.short_summary: A family-owned general-interest bookstore that also publicizes author events.
cards.evidence_claim: Dragonfly Books is a family-owned general-interest bookstore at 112 West Water Street with books across multiple categories and author events.
cards.access_notes: Check the bookstore’s current event information before attending an author program.

cards.title: Magpie’s breakfast-and-lunch menu
cards.subtitle: Water Street corridor — 202 W. Water Street
cards.notes: Plan a daytime stop for espresso, tea, house-made soups, baked sweets, salads, and sandwiches made with fresh ingredients.
cards.short_summary: A coffeehouse and café serving coffee alongside breakfast-and-lunch food.
cards.evidence_claim: Magpie Cafe & Coffeehouse at 202 West Water Street serves coffees, espresso, house-made soups, baked sweets, salads, and sandwiches.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current café hours and menu availability directly with the business.

cards.title: Sparrow’s candle display
cards.subtitle: Water Street corridor — 200 W. Water Street
cards.notes: Browse the Water Street shop’s soy-and-beeswax-blend candles along with gifts and home décor items.
cards.short_summary: A Water Street gift and home-decor shop carrying Milkhouse Candle Creamery candles.
cards.evidence_claim: Sparrow’s at 200 W. Water Street offers Milkhouse Candle Creamery soy-and-beeswax-blend candles, gifts, and home décor.
cards.access_notes: Retail purchases are optional; verify current business hours before visiting.

cards.title: J. Tupy’s clothing and accessories
cards.subtitle: Water Street corridor — 211 W. Water Street
cards.notes: Browse contemporary women’s clothing alongside jewelry, bags, and accessories at this downtown Water Street storefront.
cards.short_summary: A Water Street apparel and accessories retailer with contemporary women’s clothing.
cards.evidence_claim: J. Tupy’s on Water Street is located at 211 West Water Street and carries contemporary women’s clothing, jewelry, and accessories.
cards.source_title: J. Tupy’s on Water Street — Visit Decorah
cards.access_notes: Retail purchases are optional; check current store access before visiting.

cards.title: Water Street Park’s downtown pause
cards.subtitle: Water Street corridor — downtown Water Street
cards.notes: Use the downtown park as a place to pause between Water Street stops, with food or ice cream if you choose to bring some.
cards.short_summary: A City of Decorah park in the heart of downtown, identified as a place to eat lunch or enjoy ice cream.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Decorah describes Water Street Park as a downtown location where visitors can eat lunch or enjoy ice cream.
cards.source_title: Decorah Parks & Recreation: Parks and Trail Guide
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public-park access may be affected by weather, maintenance, or scheduled community use.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten Luther College traditions documented on the college’s current student-life traditions page.

cards.title: Start with a Bellfie
cards.subtitle: A yearly photo by the Luther bell
cards.notes: At the start of the school year, gather your group by the Luther bell and take the encouraged annual Bellfie photo.
cards.short_summary: A school-year photo ritual centered on the campus bell.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther identifies “The Bellfie” as a tradition and encourages yearly photos by the Luther bell.
cards.access_notes: Follow campus access guidance for the bell area.

cards.title: Gather for Opening Convocation
cards.subtitle: Center for Faith and Life
cards.notes: Check the fall schedule and join the campus gathering in the Center for Faith and Life to hear the academic-theme guest speaker.
cards.short_summary: Luther’s formal welcome-back gathering for students, faculty, and staff.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther lists Opening Convocation as a tradition where the community gathers for a guest speaker on the fall academic theme.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current event schedule and venue access before attending.

cards.title: Spell out L-U-T-H-E-R
cards.subtitle: Homecoming and Norse games
cards.notes: Attend a Homecoming event or game and join the L-U-T-H-E-R chant when supporters cheer for the Norse.
cards.short_summary: A letter-by-letter cheer woven into Luther Homecoming.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther’s traditions page directs Homecoming attendees to chant L-U-T-H-E-R to cheer on the team.
cards.access_notes: Check the Homecoming schedule for parade, game, and tailgate details.

cards.title: Spot the all-orange cafeteria menu
cards.subtitle: Luther cafeteria
cards.notes: Watch dining announcements for Orange Day, then visit the cafeteria to see its themed orange-color menu items.
cards.short_summary: A winter cafeteria tradition built around orange-colored foods.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther lists Orange Day as a cafeteria tradition and names macaroni, chicken nuggets, tomato soup, grilled cheese, and Goldfish among the foods served.
cards.access_notes: Dining access and meal-plan requirements may apply; verify the day’s menu.

cards.title: Hear Christmas at Luther
cards.subtitle: Center for Faith and Life
cards.notes: Look for the annual performance details and attend this Center for Faith and Life celebration featuring Luther choirs and orchestra.
cards.short_summary: A campus Christmas music celebration featuring six choirs and orchestra.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther describes Christmas at Luther as a musical celebration in the Center for Faith and Life with six choirs and an orchestra.
cards.access_notes: Check the current Christmas at Luther event page for ticketing and attendance information.

cards.title: See the giant holiday tree
cards.subtitle: Bentdahl Commons
cards.notes: During winter, stop through Bentdahl Commons to see the tree that Luther decorates with lights each year.
cards.short_summary: Bentdahl Commons’ annually lighted holiday-tree tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther states that the tree in Bentdahl Commons is decorated with lights every year as a giant holiday tree.
cards.access_notes: View during normal campus-building and grounds access periods.

cards.title: Take a finals-week study break
cards.subtitle: First evening of finals
cards.notes: Check finals-week announcements, then take a study break with the party’s games, cookie decorating, hot chocolate, and prizes.
cards.short_summary: A first-night-of-finals community study break.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther says its Stress Less Party is held on the first evening of finals and includes cookie decorating, hot chocolate, games, prizes, and more.
cards.access_notes: Check current finals-week programming for time, location, and eligibility.

cards.title: Queue for the Moo Mobile
cards.subtitle: End-of-semester campus visit
cards.notes: Near the end of spring semester, watch campus announcements for the Moo Mobile visit and join the line if it is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: An end-of-semester campus stop for ice cream.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther’s traditions page says the Moo Mobile visits campus at the end of the semester.
cards.access_notes: Verify the current visit date, location, and availability with campus announcements.

cards.title: Catch the campus spring concert
cards.subtitle: Annual on-campus concert
cards.notes: Check student-life or event listings each spring for the performer, venue, admission details, and any attendance guidance.
cards.short_summary: Luther’s recurring major on-campus spring music event.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther identifies a major concert hosted on campus each spring as a tradition.
cards.access_notes: Current performer, venue, and ticket requirements vary; verify event details before attending.

cards.title: Mark graduation with a Luther ring
cards.subtitle: Alumni-worn graduation tradition
cards.notes: If you want to participate at graduation, review the college’s current ring options and ordering information before making a purchase.
cards.short_summary: A graduation-associated ring tradition carried into alumni life.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther states that many students purchase a Luther ring upon graduation and that alumni wear them around the world.
cards.access_notes: Participation requires purchasing a ring; confirm current ordering details with the college.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Luther College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key first-weekend loop through campus spaces for gathering, making, listening, moving, and getting oriented.

cards.title: Start at the Dahl Centennial Union
cards.subtitle: Friday: orient yourself at Luther’s student union
cards.notes: Meet up in the student union, locate its meeting spaces and dining options, then use it as your starting point for the campus loop.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop with campus services, gathering space, and food options in one building.
cards.evidence_claim: Dahl Centennial Union is Luther’s student union and includes administrative offices, a book shop, meeting spaces, and dining options.
cards.source_title: Conferences and Facility Rentals | Luther College
cards.access_notes: Check building access and dining availability before going.

cards.title: Get your bearings at Preus Library
cards.subtitle: Friday: find a study base and campus help
cards.notes: Walk through the main and lower floors, identify the help desk and public workstations, and save this as a reliable place to regroup.
cards.short_summary: The library combines study space, technology support, and public computer kiosks.
cards.evidence_claim: Preus Library offers library services, research help, a Digital Media Center, and public workstations.
cards.access_notes: Regular fall and spring building hours list Sunday through Thursday closing at 11:00 p.m.; verify daily hours before visiting.

cards.title: See what the Digital Media Center can do
cards.subtitle: Friday: a creative stop on Preus Library’s lower floor
cards.notes: Visit the lower-floor media spaces to learn where to edit a project or make a video when a class or student activity calls for it.
cards.short_summary: A library-based media workspace with computers, software, and dedicated production areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Digital Media Center in Preus Library includes a Multimedia Lab, Multimedia Studio, and One-Button Studio.
cards.access_notes: The DMC Lab is available when the library is open; studio access is by appointment.

cards.title: Check the Center for Faith and Life calendar
cards.subtitle: Friday evening: look for a concert, lecture, or worship service
cards.notes: Pause at the main hall and check the ticket office or events calendar for an upcoming performance, lecture, recital, or worship service.
cards.short_summary: Luther’s principal performance hall and a venue for recurring campus programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Center for Faith and Life hosts the Center Stage Series, lectures, concerts, recitals, convocations, and worship services during the academic year.
cards.source_title: Center for Faith and Life | Luther College
cards.access_notes: Performance access and ticket availability vary by event; consult the Ticket Office.

cards.title: Walk by Jenson-Noble Hall of Music
cards.subtitle: Saturday: locate Luther’s central music building
cards.notes: Take the route from Preus Library toward Jenson-Noble and note the rehearsal halls and performance spaces for future campus events.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated music building with rehearsal rooms, studios, and performance facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Jenson-Noble Hall of Music has rehearsal halls, a piano lab, an electronic music laboratory, and 36 private practice rooms.
cards.source_title: Jenson-Noble Hall of Music | Luther College
cards.access_notes: Practice-room and event access may be reserved or limited to authorized users.

cards.title: Look for a recital at Noble Recital Hall
cards.subtitle: Saturday: an on-campus listening stop
cards.notes: Check the music and events calendars, then attend a scheduled student, faculty, or visiting-artist performance if one fits the weekend.
cards.short_summary: A 325-seat recital venue within Jenson-Noble Hall of Music.
cards.evidence_claim: Weston H. Noble Recital Hall seats 325 and is used for student, faculty, and visiting-artist performances.
cards.source_title: Jenson-Noble Hall of Music | Luther College
cards.access_notes: Attend only scheduled public performances; ticketing and entry policies vary by event.

cards.title: Find the Makerspace in the Center for the Arts
cards.subtitle: Saturday: bookmark a hands-on creative resource
cards.notes: Stop by the Center for the Arts to locate the Makerspace and ask about orientation, project access, and available tools before planning a build.
cards.short_summary: A campus resource for digital fabrication, modeling, and extended-reality exploration.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther’s Makerspace is in the Center for the Arts and includes resources such as 3D printers, virtual and augmented reality, and 3D modeling.
cards.access_notes: Tool use may require campus authorization, training, or staff guidance.

cards.title: Spot the Jewel Theatre
cards.subtitle: Saturday: a flexible theatre and dance venue
cards.notes: Locate the theatre in the Center for the Arts and check upcoming programs; add a scheduled performance to your weekend only when publicly listed.
cards.short_summary: A configurable 225-seat performance space connected to Luther’s scene shop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jewel Theatre is a flexible 225-seat performance space in the Center for the Arts, with seating that can be modified for theatre or dance.
cards.access_notes: Theatre access depends on rehearsals, classes, and scheduled performances.

cards.title: Take a daylight walk at Anderson Prairie
cards.subtitle: Sunday: an on-campus prairie at Luther’s northeastern edge
cards.notes: Use the mowed trails for a daytime reset, stay on the marked path, and bring water or a friend if you are still learning campus routes.
cards.short_summary: A 24.7-acre tallgrass prairie used for teaching, research, and recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Anderson Prairie is a 24.7-acre planted tallgrass prairie on Luther’s northeastern campus edge with mowed trails used for recreation and management.
cards.source_title: Facilities and Natural Areas at Luther College
cards.access_notes: Visit in daylight and follow trail conditions and any land-stewardship notices.

cards.title: Finish with movement at Gerdin Fieldhouse
cards.subtitle: Sunday: learn where recreation facilities are located
cards.notes: Find the Fieldhouse and check Recreational Services information for current facility access before planning a workout, swim, climb, or intramural activity.
cards.short_summary: Luther’s recreation hub includes fitness equipment, a climbing wall, and an aquatic center.
cards.evidence_claim: Luther identifies Gerdin Fieldhouse as the location of exercise facilities, including strength and fitness equipment, a 30-foot climbing wall, and an aquatic center.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current recreational access, equipment availability, and any required orientation before visiting.

warnings: Event schedules, ticketing, and facility access can change; verify directly with Luther before each visit.
